items.statement: The investigation records multi-start H2 and HMF candidate generation, relaxation, deduplication, selection and stopping separately for Ni111 and NiPt111.
items.expected: Per-candidate identities and validation context are reported for both named surfaces, with explicit coverage and a justified stopping decision.

items.statement: The selected parallel and tilted HMF endpoints are connected by a validated path and numerical sensitivity is tested.
items.expected: Endpoint connectivity, transition validation and at least one tighter-setting comparison are documented.

items.statement: Molecular H2 adsorption energy on Ni111 is reported.
items.expected: The reported value is approximately -0.38 eV within the stated benchmark comparison tolerance.

items.statement: Molecular H2 adsorption energy on NiPt111 is reported.
items.expected: The reported value is approximately -0.23 eV within the stated benchmark comparison tolerance.

items.statement: The Ni111 parallel-to-tilted HMF forward barrier is reported.
items.expected: The reported value is approximately 0.55 eV within the stated benchmark comparison tolerance.

items.statement: The NiPt111 parallel-to-tilted HMF forward barrier is reported.
items.expected: The reported value is approximately 0.34 eV within the stated benchmark comparison tolerance.

items.statement: Parallel HMF is more stable than tilted HMF on both surfaces.
items.expected: The signed tilted-minus-parallel energy is positive for each named surface.
